sites.functional_impact_measured: NOT MEASURED explicitly in the ledger clip; the construct was generated for structural/trafficking studies of TMD2 but no channel-function assay result is quoted in the ledger line.
sites.rationale: The ledger names S898 as the insertion position in ECL4 of full-length CFTR. Python verification: residue 898 = S, residue 899 = R, both within ECL4 (880–917), 19 aa from TM8 end (879) and 20 aa from TM9 start (918). The phrase 'at position S898' is slightly ambiguous (before or after S898); the most natural reading in a Gibson-assembly context is that the tag is inserted after S898, giving insert_after_residue = 898, residue_before = S, residue_after = R. This is a distinct junction from the FLAG site at N901/S902 (3 residues apart), reported by a different paper, so it is reported as a separate site. Ranked below the FLAG site because only one paper grounds it and no functional assay result is quoted. Triple HA tag (3xHA) inserted at position S898 in ECL4 of full-length CFTR by Gibson assembly to generate the TMD2-3HA construct (PMC9825563). The paper names S898 as the insertion position within ECL4. [validation: detected_only; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: The TMD2-3HA construct was generated by Gibson assembly from pBI-CMV2-CFTR and a gene block consisting of triple HA, with 3xHA positioned at position S898 in ECL4 of CFTR.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunofluorescence (non-permeabilized cells): FLAG detected on plasma membrane of wt-CFTR cells, absent in F508del cells — consistent with correct trafficking. PMC4405497 states 'cell surface localization of CFTR without altering its expression'. Function as a traffic reporter confirmed; channel function not explicitly re-measured in the tagged construct.
sites.rationale: The ledger explicitly names the junction as between Asn901 and Ser902 in ECL4 of full-length, membrane-anchored CFTR. Python verification confirms: residue 901 = N, residue 902 = S, both within the ECL4 span (880–917), 22 aa from the TM8 C-boundary (879) and 17 aa from the TM9 N-boundary (918), well clear of the ≥3 aa TM-proximity constraint. Two independent papers (PMC4356983 and PMC4405497) ground this exact junction. Surface display confirmed by non-permeabilized immunofluorescence. insert_after_residue = 901. FLAG octapeptide (DYKDDDDK) inserted between N901 and S902 in the fourth extracellular loop (ECL4) of full-length CFTR. Immunofluorescence without cell permeabilization confirmed surface display of the FLAG tag in wt-CFTR-expressing cells but not F508del-CFTR cells, validating the construct as a plasma-membrane traffic reporter. Confirmed in a second independent study (PMC4405497) using a lentiviral stable-expression system, which reports cell surface localization without altered expression. [validation: surface_only; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: Additionally, a Flag sequence (DYKDDDDK) was inserted between Asn901 and Ser902, i.e., in the fourth extracellular loop of CFTR ( Fig. 1a–c ).

sites.functional_impact_measured: PMC10622324: extracellular (non-lytic) bioluminescence assay detects only surface HiBiT-CFTR; total and PM pools quantified. PMC12932761: luminescence signal comparable to parental cells under vehicle (negligible PM expression of G542X), validating surface-detection sensitivity. Channel function not re-measured in the tagged constructs per the ledger clips.
sites.rationale: Two independent papers confirm HiBiT insertion in ECL4 of full-length, membrane-anchored CFTR with surface detection validated by non-lytic bioluminescence. Neither paper names the specific junction residue in the ledger clips, so this is reported as a region-level site (ECL4, residues 880–917). The exact junction cannot be pinned without inventing a position. Ranked below the residue-level sites. insert_after_residue = null; region = ECL4. HiBiT tag knocked into ECL4 of endogenous WT-CFTR at two candidate positions via CRISPR/Cas9 (PMC10622324); bioluminescence-based quantification of total and plasma-membrane CFTR confirmed. A second study (PMC12932761) used HiBiT in the extracellular domain of full-length G542X-CFTR in stable BEAS-2B cells, referencing the same ECL4 approach. Neither ledger line names the specific junction residue(s). [validation: surface_only; position: inferred; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: We investigated two potential positions for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knock-in of HiBiT in the ECL4 of WT-CFTR ( Fig 1A ) for bioluminescence-based quantification of both total endogenous levels (lytic assay) and live-cell detection of WT-CFTR in the PM (extracellular assay).

literature_notes: Four ledger entries were excluded: (1) mCherry fused to the N-terminus of CFTR (PMC4356983, PMC8976878) — the CFTR N-terminus (residues 1–77) is INTRACELLULAR per the authoritative topology landmarks; this is not an extracellular tag and does not qualify. (2) Dual-SpyTagged CFTR with C-terminal GFP (PMC13056111) — the C-terminus (residues 1148–1480) is INTRACELLULAR; both the N- and C-terminal SpyTag/GFP fusions are on the cytoplasmic face and do not qualify for extracellular-face tagging, despite the electrophysiology confirming functional preservation. All three reported sites are in ECL4 (880–917), the only extracellular loop of CFTR with published tolerated insertions in the ledger. The other extracellular loops (ECL1 94–124, ECL2 219–222, ECL3 325–347, ECL5 1012, ECL6 1122–1126) have no qualifying ledger evidence.
